pages.label: Page 6
pages.title: The Triumph of the Name of Jesus — Giovanni Battista Gaulli

pages.label: Page 7
pages.title: In the Beginning
pages.text:
JOHN 1:1, 3–5, 11–12, 14
In the Beginning
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was
with God, and the Word was God.
All things were made through him. Without him,
nothing was made that has been made. In him was
life, and the life was the light of men. The light
shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not
overcome it.
He came to his own people, but they did not receive
him. But to all those who did receive him and
believe in his name, he gave the right to become
children of God.
And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us.
Giovanni Battista Gaulli
The Triumph of the Name of Jesus, 1676–1679
Chiesa del Gesù, Rome (Source and full credit: p. 48)

pages.label: Page 8
pages.title: The Annunciation
pages.text:
LUKE 1:26–29
The Annunciation
The angel Gabriel was sent by God to Nazareth,
a city of Galilee, to a virgin betrothed to a
man named Joseph, of the house of David. And the
virgin’s name was Mary.
The angel came to her and said, “Greetings, you who
are full of grace! The Lord is with you.”
Mary was greatly troubled by these words and
wondered what kind of greeting this might be.
Sandro Botticelli
The Cestello Annunciation, 1489–1490
Gallerie degli Uffizi, Florence

pages.label: Page 10
pages.title: Annunciation with Saint Maxima (traditionally Margaret) and Saint Ansanus — Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi

pages.label: Page 11
pages.title: Do Not Be Afraid
pages.text:
LUKE 1:30–33
Do Not Be Afraid
The angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary,
for you have found favor with God.
“Behold, you will conceive in your womb and give
birth to a son and shall name him Jesus. He will be
great and will be called the Son of the Most High.
“The Lord God will give him the throne of his father
David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob
forever. And his kingdom will have no end.”
Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi
Annunciation with Saint Maxima (traditionally Margaret) and Saint Ansanus, 1333
Gallerie degli Uffizi, Florence

pages.label: Page 12
pages.title: Let It Be Done
pages.text:
LUKE 1:34–38
Let It Be Done
Mary said to the angel, “How can this be since I
am a virgin?”
The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come
upon you, and the power of the Most High will
overshadow you. Therefore, the child born of you will
be called holy and the Son of God.
“Behold, Elizabeth your relative also has conceived
a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month with
her who was called barren. For nothing is impossible
with God.”
Mary said, “Behold, I am the servant of the Lord; let
it be done to me according to your word.” Then the
angel departed from her.
Henry Ossawa Tanner
The Annunciation, 1898
Philadelphia Museum of Art

pages.label: Page 14
pages.title: The Dream of Saint Joseph — Philippe de Champaigne

pages.label: Page 15
pages.title: The Dream of Joseph
pages.text:
MATTHEW 1:18–21
The Dream of Joseph
When Mary was betrothed to Joseph, but
before they came together, she was found
to be with child by the Holy Spirit. Her husband
Joseph, being a just man and not wanting to put her
to shame, decided to divorce her quietly.
But as he considered these things, behold, an
angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream
saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to
take to yourself Mary as your wife, for that which is
conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
“She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him
Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”
Philippe de Champaigne
The Dream of Saint Joseph, 1642–1643
The National Gallery, London

pages.label: Page 16
pages.title: Call Him Immanuel
pages.text:
MATTHEW 1:22–24
Call Him Immanuel
All of this took place to fulfill what the Lord
spoke through the prophet, “Behold, the
virgin shall be with child and give birth to a son.
They shall call him Immanuel,” which means, “God
with us.”
Joseph arose from his sleep and did as the angel of
the Lord commanded and took his wife to himself.
Raphael
The Marriage of the Virgin, 1504
Pinacoteca di Brera, Milan

pages.label: Page 17
pages.title: The Marriage of the Virgin — Raphael

pages.label: Page 19
pages.title: The Visitation
pages.text:
LUKE 1:39–45
The Visitation
Mary arose and went with haste to the hill
country to a city of Judah, and she entered
the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby
leapt in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the
Holy Spirit.
She called out with a loud voice, “Blessed are you
among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
Why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord
should come to me? For behold, when the voice of
your greeting came to my ears, the baby leapt in my
womb for joy!
“Blessed is she who believed that there would be a
fulfillment of the things which have been spoken to
her from the Lord.”
Domenico Ghirlandaio
The Visitation, 1491
Musée du Louvre, Paris

pages.label: Page 20
pages.title: My Soul Magnifies the Lord
pages.text:
LUKE 1:46–55
My Soul
Magnifies the Lord
Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord! My
spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has
looked at the humble state of his servant. From now
on, all generations will call me blessed.
“For he who is mighty has done great things for me.
Holy is his name. His mercy is for generations and
generations on those who fear him.
“He has shown strength with his arm. He has
scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
He has put down princes from their thrones and has
exalted the lowly. He has filled the hungry with good
things. He has sent the rich away empty.
“He has given help to Israel, his servant, that he
might remember mercy, as he spoke to our fathers, to
Abraham and his descendants forever.”
Titian
Assumption of the Virgin, 1516–1518
Basilica di Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, Venice

pages.label: Page 22
pages.title: The Age of Augustus, the Birth of Christ — Jean-Léon Gérôme

pages.label: Page 23
pages.title: Everyone to His Own City
pages.text:
LUKE 2:1–5
Everyone to
His Own City
Now in those days, a decree went out from
Caesar Augustus that all the world should
be registered. This was the first census made when
Quirinius was governor of Syria. All went to be
registered, each to his own city.
Joseph went out from Nazareth in Galilee into
Judea to Bethlehem, the city of David, because he
was of the house and family of David. He went to
register himself with Mary, his betrothed, who was
with child.
Jean-Léon Gérôme
The Age of Augustus, the Birth of Christ, c. 1852–1854
J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles

pages.label: Page 24
pages.title: The Birth of Christ
pages.text:
LUKE 2:6–7
The Birth of Christ
While they were there, the day had come
for her to give birth. She gave birth to her
firstborn son.
She wrapped him in swaddling clothes and laid him
in a manger, because there was no room for them in
the inn.
Carlo Maratta
The Holy Night, c. 1656
Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden

pages.label: Page 26
pages.title: The Angel Appearing to the Shepherds — Thomas Cole

pages.label: Page 27
pages.title: Glory to God in the Highest
pages.text:
LUKE 2:8–14
Glory to God
in the Highest
There were shepherds in the same country
staying in the field and keeping watch by
night over their flock. Behold, an angel of the Lord
appeared to them, and the glory of the Lord shone
around them, and they were terrified.
The angel said to them, “Do not be afraid, for
behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will
be for all the people. For there is born to you today, in
the city of David, a Savior who is Christ the Lord.
“This will be a sign for you: you will find a baby
wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in a manger.”
Suddenly, there appeared alongside the angel a
multitude of the heavenly army praising God,
“Glory to God in the highest! And on earth peace,
good will toward men.”
Thomas Cole
The Angel Appearing to the Shepherds, 1833–1834
Chrysler Museum of Art, Norfolk, VA

pages.label: Page 28
pages.title: They Went with Haste
pages.text:
LUKE 2:15–20
They Went with Haste
When the angels went away from them into
heaven, the shepherds said to one another,
“Let us go to Bethlehem now and see this thing that
has happened which the Lord has made known to
us.” They went with haste and found Mary and
Joseph; and the baby was lying in the manger.
When they saw him, they told everyone what was
spoken to them about the child.
All who heard it wondered at what the shepherds
told them. But Mary treasured all these things,
pondering them in her heart.
The shepherds returned glorifying and praising
God for all the things that they had heard and seen,
just as it was told them.
Gerrit van Honthorst
The Adoration of the Shepherds, 1622
Wallraf-Richartz-Museum, Cologne

pages.label: Page 29
pages.title: The Adoration of the Shepherds — Gerrit van Honthorst

pages.label: Page 30
pages.title: Journey of the Magi — James Tissot

pages.label: Page 31
pages.title: Wise Men from the East
pages.text:
MATTHEW 2:1–4
Wise Men from the East
When Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in
the days of King Herod, behold, wise men
from the east came to Jerusalem saying, “Where is
he who is born King of the Jews? For we saw his star
when it rose and have come to worship him.”
When King Herod heard it, he was troubled, and all
Jerusalem with him.
Gathering together all the chief priests and scribes
of the people, he asked them where the Christ was
to be born.
James Tissot
Journey of the Magi, c. 1894
Minneapolis Institute of Art

pages.label: Page 32
pages.title: In Bethlehem of Judea
pages.text:
MATTHEW 2:5–8
In Bethlehem of Judea
They said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this
is written by the prophet, ‘You Bethlehem, in the
land of Judah, are in no way least among the rulers
of Judah; for out of you shall come a ruler who will
shepherd my people Israel. ’”
Then Herod secretly summoned the wise men and
learned from them when the star had appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Go and
search diligently for the child. When you have found
him, bring me word, so that I also may come and
worship him.”
Domenico Ghirlandaio
The Adoration of the Magi, 1488–1489
Museo degli Innocenti, Florence

pages.label: Page 33
pages.title: The Adoration of the Magi — Domenico Ghirlandaio

pages.label: Page 34
pages.title: The Adoration of the Magi — Gentile da Fabriano

pages.label: Page 35
pages.title: Gold, Frankincense, & Myrrh
pages.text:
MATTHEW 2:9–12
Gold, Frankincense,
& Myrrh
Having heard the king, they went on their way.
And behold, the star, which they saw when it
rose, went before them until it came and stood over
where the young child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with
exceedingly great joy. They came into the house and
saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and
they fell down and worshiped him.
Opening their treasures, they offered him gifts:
gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Being warned in a dream not to return to Herod,
they went back to their own country another way.
Gentile da Fabriano
The Adoration of the Magi, 1423
Gallerie degli Uffizi, Florence

pages.label: Page 36
pages.title: The Presentation
pages.text:
LUKE 2:21–22, 25–26
The Presentation
On the eighth day when he was circumcised, he
was named Jesus, the name given by the angel
before he was conceived in the womb.
When the days of their purification according to the
law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him up to
Jerusalem to present him to the Lord.
There was a man in Jerusalem whose name was
Simeon. He was righteous and devout, waiting for
the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was
upon him. It had been revealed to him by the Holy
Spirit that he should not see death before he had
seen the Lord’s Christ.
James Tissot
Reconstruction of Jerusalem and the Temple of Herod, 1886–1894
Brooklyn Museum, New York

pages.label: Page 37
pages.title: Reconstruction of Jerusalem and the Temple of Herod — James Tissot

pages.label: Page 38
pages.title: The Presentation in the Temple — Philippe de Champaigne

pages.label: Page 39
pages.title: My Eyes Have Seen Your Salvation
pages.text:
LUKE 2:27–32
My Eyes Have
Seen Your Salvation
Simeon came in the Spirit into the temple. When
the parents brought in the child Jesus, that they
might do for him according to the custom of the law,
he took him in his arms and blessed God saying,
“Lord, now you may let your servant go in peace,
according to your word. For my eyes have seen your
salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of
all peoples, a light for revelation to the nations, and
for the glory of your people Israel.”
Philippe de Champaigne
The Presentation in the Temple, 1648
Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels

pages.label: Page 40
pages.title: A Sword Will Pierce Your Heart
pages.text:
LUKE 2:33–35
A Sword Will
Pierce Your Heart
Joseph and Mary were marveling at the things
which were spoken about him.
Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, his mother,
“Behold, this child is appointed for the falling and
rising of many in Israel and to be a sign which is
spoken against.
“A sword will pierce your heart also. And the thoughts
of many hearts will be revealed.”
William-Adolphe Bouguereau
The Virgin with Angels, 1900
Petit Palais, Paris

pages.label: Page 41
pages.title: The Virgin with Angels — William-Adolphe Bouguereau

pages.label: Page 43
pages.title: Flight to Egypt
pages.text:
MATTHEW 2:13–15
Flight to Egypt
Behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph
in a dream saying, “Arise and take the young
child and his mother and flee to Egypt and stay there
until I tell you, for Herod will seek the young child to
destroy him.”
He arose and took the young child and his mother
by night and departed to Egypt and was there until
the death of Herod.
This fulfilled what was spoken by the Lord through
the prophet, “Out of Egypt, I have called my son.”
Eugène Girardet
Flight into Egypt, 1883
Private collection

pages.label: Page 44
pages.title: A City Called Nazareth
pages.text:
MATTHEW 2:19–23
A City Called Nazareth
When Herod was dead, behold, an angel of
the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in
Egypt saying, “Arise and take the young child and
his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who
sought the young child’s life are dead.”
So he arose and took the young child and his
mother and went to the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over
Judea in the place of his father Herod, he was afraid
to go there.
Being warned in a dream, he withdrew into Galilee
and settled in a city called Nazareth, that it might
be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophets
that he will be called a Nazarene.
Bartolomé Esteban Murillo
The Holy Family with a Little Bird, c. 1650
Museo Nacional del Prado, Madrid

pages.label: Page 45
pages.title: The Holy Family with a Little Bird — Bartolomé Esteban Murillo

pages.label: Page 47
pages.title: The Grace of God Was Upon Him
pages.text:
LUKE 2:39–40
The Grace of God
Was Upon Him
When they had accomplished everything
according to the law of the Lord, they
returned to Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong, filled with
wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
Raphael
The Canigiani Holy Family, c. 1505–1506
Alte Pinakothek, Munich
